EBOOKS · IN ISPUTNIK.HOME

Every book in the house.
Open right where you stopped.

EPUB, FB2 and PDF files become a library with covers, authors and series, and a reader in the browser that keeps your page on every device. Send a book to your e-reader whenever you like.

Get iSputnik ↗See what it does ↓
  • No cloud needed
  • No ads
  • No hidden costs
  • No tracking

WHAT IT DOES

From the shelf to your e-reader.

Read

A reader in the browser — nothing to install.

  • EPUB and FB2 in the built-in reader
  • Font, size, spacing and theme, kept from book to book
  • Your place saved per book and per person
  • Bookmarks, and highlights of the passages that matter
  • PDFs open in the browser’s own viewer

Keep what you read

The best lines shouldn’t stay inside one book.

  • Select a passage and keep it as a quote
  • Every quote and highlight, across all your books
  • A quote of the day on Home
  • Reviews with stars on the book’s page

Take it with you

Read here, or wherever you like to read.

  • Download the original file
  • Send it to your Kindle or Kobo by email
  • Reading apps like KOReader, Moon+ Reader and Thorium, over OPDS
  • Pass a book to someone in the family
  • Downloaded books stay readable offline

A tidy library

The library sorts itself out, and asks before it changes much.

  • One file, one book — details from the file itself
  • The EPUB and PDF of one book become one title
  • Editions — a translation, the audiobook — grouped on one page
  • Authors, series, categories and an A–Z index
  • Anything deleted waits in the recycle bin

PRIVATE HERE, SPECIFICALLY

What you read is nobody’s data.

The general promises hold everywhere. These are the ones that matter most for ebooks.

Your reading stays at home

Your page in every book, your highlights and your quotes are kept on your own server. No store is watching what you read, or for how long.

Reading apps get a key, not your password

An OPDS app signs in with a reader token you make in your profile — and can take back in one click.

Your e-reader, through your own mail

Send to Kindle or Kobo goes out through the mail server you set up. Nobody in between keeps a copy.

Your files are only read

Titles and covers come from the files; your corrections are kept in iSputnik and survive every re-scan.

WORKS WITH

Books connect to everything else.

AudiobooksOwn the ebook and the audiobook? They sit together as editions of one book. StoriesReviews with stars, and book cards placed right inside a story. Photos & home videoA book, its quotes and the photos that go with it can share a collection.

WHAT YOU NEED

Your books and a browser.

iSputnik.home
Ebooks are part of it. Point an ebook library at your folder of EPUB, FB2 and PDF files.
Send to e-reader optional
Mail set up on the server, and your Kindle or Kobo address in your profile. The device has to approve the server’s sender address.
A reading app optional
KOReader, Moon+ Reader, Thorium or any app that speaks OPDS.

QUESTIONS

About ebooks.

More in the Ebooks guide and Quotes.

Does a PDF remember my page?

No — PDFs open in the browser’s own viewer, which keeps no reading position and no highlights. That’s the format, not the app. If you have the EPUB too, read that.

Can I read on my Kindle or Kobo?

Yes. Send to → My e-reader mails the book to your device once mail is set up on the server. Or use an OPDS app like KOReader to browse and download the library yourself.

I have the same book as EPUB and PDF. Two entries?

One. Files with the same name in the same folder become one book offering both formats.

What if I delete a book by mistake?

It goes to the recycle bin, not away for good, and can be restored until the bin is emptied.
